28 A tube of length L is open at both ends. A stationary wave is set up in this tube when a tuning fork
vibrating with frequency fx is held at one end. This is the lowest frequency of stationary wave that
can be formed in this tube.
Another tube of length 2L is closed at one end. A stationary wave is set up in this tube when a
tuning fork vibrating with frequency fy is held at the open end. This is the lowest frequency of
stationary wave that can be formed in this tube.
frequency fx
L
frequency fy
2L
Assume the end correction for each tube is negligible.
Which equation is correct?
yf
C
fx = 2fy
D
fx = 4fy
A
fx = 4
yf
B
fx = 2

hints: Notice the two tubes differ in both length, $L$ against $2L$, and in end conditions, open at both ends against closed at one end.
Recall the fundamental wavelength fits half a wavelength in an open-open tube but only a quarter wavelength in a closed-open tube.
Write $f_x = v/\lambda_x$ with $\lambda_x$ from $L$, and $f_y = v/\lambda_y$ with $\lambda_y$ from $2L$, then form the ratio $f_x/f_y$.
walkthrough: For the tube of length $L$ open at both ends, both ends are displacement antinodes. The lowest frequency fits half a wavelength: $L = \lambda_x/2$, so $\lambda_x = 2L$.
Its fundamental frequency is $f_x = v/\lambda_x = v/(2L)$, where $v$ is the speed of sound.
For the tube of length $2L$ closed at one end, the closed end is a node and the open end is an antinode. The lowest frequency fits a quarter wavelength: $2L = \lambda_y/4$, so $\lambda_y = 8L$.
Its fundamental frequency is $f_y = v/\lambda_y = v/(8L)$.

A.explanation: This would make $f_x$ much smaller than $f_y$, but the open tube of length $L$ has a much shorter fundamental wavelength than the closed tube of length $2L$.

B.explanation: This would make $f_x$ smaller than $f_y$, which reverses the physics: a shorter open pipe cannot have a lower fundamental frequency than a longer closed pipe.

C.explanation: This accounts for only one effect, the doubled length $2L$, but misses the extra factor of 2 from open-open compared with closed-open end conditions.

D.explanation: With $\lambda_x = 2L$ and $\lambda_y = 8L$, $f_x = v/(2L)$ is four times $f_y = v/(8L)$.
